note: The floors are the census sizes measured on the run that wrote them, and they are a ratchet
rather than a guess. A layer that reads fewer rows than its floor exits 3, not 0: a shrunken
denominator raises reported coverage while measuring less.
SIX DECLARED DIVERGENCES. Every citation in harnesses.pairing.tsv opens with `Dn · `, naming
the one it falls under. A finding whose citation carries no number, or a number this list does
not define, is a defect. The split is countable off the run's own artifact:
F='| \(absent\|divergent\|extra\|extra-cited\|unclassified\) |'
grep -c "$F" planning/fidelity/harnesses.ledger.md
grep "$F" planning/fidelity/harnesses.ledger.md | grep -c '| D[0-9] ·'
1. THE MOCK DRAWS A VERSION ON EVERY ROW AND THE BUILD DRAWS NONE. Owner: M22, parked.
`~/.claude.json · v2.1.204` and its five siblings. Nothing in this product observes a
harness's installed version. The nearest thing is HTTPCapability's `codex 0.146.0`, which
names the binary a probe was taken against on 2026-08-21 rather than the one on this
machine, so rendering it as a version would be a claim about the user's install that
nothing measured — DESIGN.md §6. Getting it honestly means spawning each harness binary
with --version on every board refresh. Parked in planning/plans/plan-M22.md §2.2 with that
reason rather than filled in with something plausible.
2. THE RECONCILE PANEL IS A HOLE THIS BOARD OWNS. Owner: M22, and that is the record rather
than a hand-off. The brief gives the finding an action that opens the diff of the real file,
and gives a duplicating row its own. Both controls are DRAWN and DISABLED with the reason in
their help tag, per DESIGN.md §3.4 — a disabled control dims in place with a discoverable
reason and never disappears.
`RouterSheet.Kind.reconcile` on ai/m18 at 6721e5c carries `owner: "M22"`, and
RouterSheetTests.unhostedKindsAreTheOnesOnRecord asserts it stays in the UNHOSTED set: the
mock draws the sheet, the build does not host it, and M22 owns the gap. Hosting it is what
would break that test. So HarnessesBoardModel.Sheet deliberately carries no reconcile case —
an unreachable one would read as an intention to host. That type does not exist on this
branch, so nothing here is compiled against it; the alignment is a merge-time obligation and
is recorded in planning/progress/M22.md.
Both controls were briefly ENABLED buttons setting a sheet state nothing presented, which is
the worse of the two failures because it looked like it worked: the click succeeded, the
state changed, and nothing appeared.
NEITHER IS A PRIMARY, AND §3.4 IS WHY RATHER THAN CARE. The mock cannot express a disabled
primary at all — .btn:disabled at design/mcp-router-console.html:679 and .btn.primary at :680
are both specificity 0-2-0 and .primary is declared second, so it wins on background,
border-color and color, and a disabled primary keeps its accent fill and its --on-accent
label (measured independently by two sessions on 2026-08-22). The collision cannot arise on
this board because §3.4 allows one prominent accent-filled action per view: every disabled
control here is a StandardButtonStyle by construction, not by having avoided the trap.
3. PER-ROW COUNT PILLS AND `Verify now`. Owner: M22, declined. The mock's rows carry
`135 tools reachable`, `0 processes at rest` and `Verified 3 min ago` as pills. The first
two are Servers-board figures attributed to a harness — the router serves one tool surface
to every harness, so `135 tools reachable` is the same number on every row and says nothing
about the row it sits on. `Verify now` is a per-harness re-read; the board reads every
harness in one call, so the control it earns is the board-level `Check again`, which is
built. The freshness the mock puts on each row is on the footer instead, once, from the
route's own readAt.
4. `Wire to the router` AND `Choose a config file…`. Owner: R7 §7 / A36. Both write or select
a harness configuration file. scripts/lint/no-harness-config-writes.sh keeps the
reconciliation seam free of any writer, and there is no applier anywhere in the product; a
button offering to write one would be the first. Not drawn at all rather than drawn dim,
because dim-with-a-reason says `not yet` and the answer here is `not from this app`.
5. THE MOCK'S `Not found` SECTION. Owner: M22, folded. It draws one card explaining that
Claude Desktop cannot be wired. The route reports every harness in MCPClient.allCases with
its own `exists` and `unreadable`, so a harness that is not installed is a row rather than
a prose paragraph, and the capability sentence on the row carries the same fact with its
provenance attached.
7. THE 44 UNCLASSIFIED ROWS, SPLIT BY WHETHER VOUCHING THEM WOULD MEASURE ANYTHING.
`unclassified` here is D-m23-h, not a defect in this surface: VOUCHED_CONTROLS covers the
six mock kinds the one filled ledger paired, and its own comment says the first surface to
pair another reads it as a finding until the pairing is vouched. This is that surface. The
split matters more than the total, and it was measured off this run's own ledger rather
than argued:
10 of 44 WOULD MEASURE NOTHING IF VOUCHED. Both sides carry no text, so the engine's
`present if mock_text == app_text` would fire on two empty strings — agreement between
two absences, which is the defect VOUCHED_CONTROLS was built to stop and which its header
names in those words. indicator<-status-indicator (6), icon<-finding-icon (1),
icon<-state-illustration (1), card<-skeleton-card (2). Vouching any of them buys a green
row that establishes nothing.
34 of 44 WOULD MEASURE SOMETHING. Both sides carry text: banner, button, callout, card,
heading, section-header and sentence against this board's roles. Those are real pairings
and the table is where they would be recorded.
THE TABLE IS NOT EDITED HERE, for two reasons and the second is the binding one. It is
M23's oracle, and widening it so this surface goes green is the shape of edit it exists to
prevent. And it is already moving: M16 has scripts/acceptance/mock_fidelity.py at +18/-1 on
ai/m16 from this same base — adding `signature` to `card` and a `jack` entry, and leaving
`indicator` deliberately absent with the reason written out, which is the same reason the
first bucket above gives. Two items editing one dict from one base is a merge conflict in a
file whose job is to be the oracle. Raised as a sequencing question rather than resolved.
ONE OF THE TEN IS NOT ABOUT THE TABLE AT ALL: icon<-state-illustration is ALREADY vouched
(mock_fidelity.py:68) and still reads unclassified, so its cause is the comparable-
granularity gate rather than the vouching table. Recorded because the open question had two
causes in it and only one of them is VOUCHED_CONTROLS.
6. THE ERROR FRAME IS A PARTIAL READ, NOT A FAILED ONE. Owner: M22, deliberate. The mock's
v-error draws a banner over a callout saying the other five harnesses were read normally,
which is DESIGN.md §5's `partial` rather than its `error`. MeasureDump maps
(.harnesses, .error) to the `partial` fixture for exactly that reason; the router-not-
running state is rendered from ControlAPIError and is not one of the mock's four frames.

layers.name: font-weight-face
layers.substitute: A SwiftUI Font is opaque — String(describing: Font.system(size: 13, weight: .semibold)) returns "Font(provider: SwiftUI.FontBox<SwiftUI.Font.SystemProvider>)", with no size, weight or face in it. Confirmed instead by: the TypeToken each text node names is recorded in tokens["type"] at apply time and checked against the measured line box by the type-metrics layer; DesignTokenParityTests pins the eight-role ladder against DESIGN.md; scripts/lint/no-raw-design-values.sh fails any font size that does not come off it. None of the three can see an ancestor .font() winning the cascade, and that residue is what this row is.
